- The speaker begins by stating that "delivering education of our smartphone is like hoping that people will eat their broccoli but right next to it you put the most delicious dessert ever made" (0:00-0:10).
- The speaker emphasizes that to "really want to deliver education to everyone," it must not only be accessible but also make people "want to actually learn" (0:10-0:17).
- The speaker then says, "and at the highest level the way we've done this is by making the broccoli tastes like dessert" (0:17-0:22).
- The speaker asks, "you know what is the best time to send people a notification" (0:22-0:25).
- The speaker answers their own question, stating, "I'll tell you it's 24 hours after they use the product last because there's an easy explanation if you were free yesterday at 3 p.m. you probably free today at 3 p.m. as well" (0:25-0:35).
- The speaker mentions that "this is what a very sophisticated millions of dollars of AI found" (0:35-0:38).
- The speaker explains that "these passive aggressive notifications are really good at getting people to come back because they feel like our Green Owl mascot has given up on them" (0:38-0:46).
- The speaker suggests that "if we want to get people to do something meaningful you can use the same techniques that apps like social media use to get people to do it" (0:46-0:53).
- The speaker concludes by saying, "and even if you're not as engaging as those apps are you can still get hundreds of millions of people to use your product" (0:53-0:59).

- The speaker mentions that many people have been asking when the next "cozy lease sale event" is, and while she wishes it were tomorrow, things need to be done sustainably and healthily for it to happen.
- The speaker explains that their "homework Chef" got "pretty messy" during and after their first sale event, which is why they are now renovating their workshop to fix it.
- The speaker emphasizes the importance of everyone being on the same page for a big project like this and offers a "behind the scenes" look at their process.
- The team is using "slack canvas" to help manage the project, which the speaker describes as a great way to add structure and documentation.
- To kick off the project, they made a canvas to highlight general tasks and assigned roles to each other.
- They decided to build separate workshop stations for woodworking, 3D printing, and ceramics for some upcoming projects.
- The speaker notes that their canvas is "looking so nice" and is "so informative."
- The speaker encourages viewers to follow along with their workshop renovation journey and to check out "slack canvas" if they are interested in a tool to improve team documentation, communication, and productivity.
